paths.description: Homepage and global WordPress template: navigation, consent, content discovery, privacy, performance and preferences.
Tourism category listing, representing editorial index/archive templates.
Long tourism article with carousel, representing content/detail templates and mobile reflow risk.
Cinema listing and selector, representing a separate interactive listing/application template.
GET search-results journey from the global search form, representing task completion and empty/result state handling.
Fabricated missing route to inspect HTTP/error recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in layout and light surfaces to the default capture; the CSS feature probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule or color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define light/dark surface and text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), checking third-party UI integration too.

findings.summary: The rendered interface does not survive increased-contrast emulation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is an effectively blank brown viewport, while the default capture contains navigation and the consent dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Test forced-colors and prefers-contrast states, retain semantic borders/text, and avoid colour overrides that erase controls or content.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes use abrupt legacy swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/platform probe found no view-transition rules; representative pages are separate full document loads and the cinema accordion uses legacy Bootstrap collapse.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article/category navigation and same-document transitions for menus, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The fixed navigation chrome does not respond to scroll position.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show a fixed, full-height header; the CSS feature probe found no scroll-state/container query or progress affordance on long pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight progress/shrinking-header treatment on long articles, with a non-supporting-browser fallback.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the full page before the user can read any content.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, category, article, search and 404 screenshots all open behind a viewport-blocking consent dialog. On mobile it occupies nearly the entire 360×800 viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with the least intrusive legally compliant consent pattern possible, keep reject and accept equally prominent, preserve page headings outside the modal, and ensure dismissal persists securely.

findings.summary: Site overlays are custom div-based dialogs rather than native top-layer primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found event and consent overlays implemented as div[role=dialog], with no native dialog or popover element.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal flows and popover for transient UI, relying on native focus management, Escape handling and light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: The representative article breaks mobile reflow with a desktop-width layout.
findings.evidence: At a 360×800 viewport the article layout reports scrollWidth 1165px, horizontal overflow of 805px, innerWidth 1165px and CLS 0.447.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed/minimum desktop widths from the article and carousel, use intrinsic responsive sizing and max-inline-size:100%, and verify every article template at 320–400 CSS px.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation adapt only through legacy viewport layout rules.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no @container rules; the WordPress and cinema templates use global Bootstrap/grid breakpoints despite components appearing in main and sidebar contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for repeated cards, media rows and navigation modules so each component responds to its available inline size.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the primary navigation.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing the visible “Loterías” link produced outline "none" and box-shadow "none".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring with sufficient offset for links, buttons, menu triggers and form controls; never remove outlines without an equivalent.

findings.summary: Every primary content journey begins with a blocking consent detour.
findings.evidence: The consent wall appears before the homepage, category, article, search and 404 paths, preventing immediate access to articles, lottery information and recovery content.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the consent interruption, retain readable underlying purpose, and let users reject in one action without changing heading hierarchy or delaying the requested content.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is outside the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.2s, LCP 5.6s, Speed Index 14.6s and Time to Interactive 20.2s (performance score 0.57). The raw-CDP trace corroborated an LCP of 2.34s under its lighter desktop condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, delay advertising/analytics until after content and consent, reduce render-blocking CSS/JS, and monitor field LCP and INP.

findings.summary: The article template has severe mobile layout shift.
findings.evidence: The article mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.447, dominated by a 0.445 shift around 5 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for carousel, ad and media regions; set image dimensions/aspect-ratio; and use stable font fallbacks so late content cannot move the article.

findings.summary: The critical path is crowded by blocking styles/scripts and weak caching.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 108 requests and 2.43MB. It identified eight parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets plus synchronous head scripts, and many first-party CSS/JS assets without useful cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, conditionally load plugin styles, defer non-critical scripts, remove synchronous head dependencies, and add long-lived immutable caching to versioned assets.

findings.summary: Most shipped frontend code is unused on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 787KiB unused JavaScript and 99KiB unused CSS; examples include Taboola, ad stacks, Facebook, Chart.js, mediaelement and WordPress block/dashicon CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load plugins and ad vendors only on routes and after states that need them, remove duplicate ad loaders, split bundles, and purge unused WordPress CSS.

findings.summary: Social links have no accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the DOM accessibility probe identified the Facebook, Twitter and Instagram icon-only anchors as focusable but unnamed.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only link a concise aria-label or visible text, keeping decorative icons aria-hidden.

findings.summary: Text in the footer and consent interface fails WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the footer link at 2.69:1 and several consent controls between 1.06:1 and 2.8:1, below the 4.5:1 text requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens and overlay compositing so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and essential UI remains perceivable in every dialog state.

findings.summary: The content heading structure is displaced by the consent UI and visible focus is absent.
findings.evidence: The homepage authored DOM has no content h1, while the loaded page exposes consent/vendor headings as multiple h1/h2 elements; the first visible navigation link has no focus indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one descriptive page h1 per template outside overlays, keep dialog headings scoped below it, use semantic landmarks, and restore visible focus.

findings.summary: The article cannot reflow at a standard mobile width.
findings.evidence: At 360px the article is 1165px wide with 805px horizontal overflow, forcing two-dimensional scrolling and preventing normal zoom/reflow use.
findings.suggestedFix: Refactor fixed-width wrappers and media to fluid logical sizing; test WCAG reflow at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Images and assets are not consistently sized for sound rendering.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 4/8 images without dimensions, 5/8 without srcset, 5 legacy-format images and 3 below-fold images not lazy-loaded. Lighthouse also found low-resolution rendered images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or aspect-ratio), responsive srcset/sizes, appropriate intrinsic resolutions, modern formats and loading=lazy for below-fold images.

findings.summary: Search results omit a meta description.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM summaries show descriptive title/description pairs on home, category and article paths, but the representative ?s=playa search result has no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise query-aware description for search/listing templates while retaining unique titles.

findings.summary: The cinema template omits a canonical link.
findings.evidence: The WordPress home/category/article pages expose canonical URLs, but the separately rendered cinema listing DOM has no rel=canonical despite returning indexable content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referencing canonical to the cinema listing and detail templates, and keep it consistent with sitemap and status signals.

findings.summary: The cinema listing lacks structured/share metadata despite representing a rich entity collection.
findings.evidence: Home and WordPress article templates contain JSON-LD, while the cinema listing has no JSON-LD and no canonical in its rendered head.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate BreadcrumbList/CollectionPage or ItemList JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata that matches the visible cinema and movie content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but key security headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: The header primitive found no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options. The FCCDCF cookie is not Secure, uses SameSite=None and lasts 390 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, HSTS and nosniff; review the consent cookie so SameSite and Secure are appropriate and its lifetime is minimised.

findings.summary: The page has a disproportionate tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 26 third-party origins and five known trackers. The HAR attributed 76 requests and 2.07MB to third parties, while the consent UI lists 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors to those necessary, block all non-essential requests before consent, batch/minimise analytics, and document a data-retention purpose for each remaining origin.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: X-Frame-Options is present, but HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, an enforcing CSP including frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and underserves some displays.
findings.evidence: Five of eight inspected images use legacy JPG/PNG, five lack responsive sources, three below-fold images are eager, and Lighthouse found low-resolution images scaled beyond their natural size.
findings.suggestedFix: Create AVIF/WebP variants, provide srcset/sizes at appropriate resolutions, lazy-load below-fold media, and preserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Advertising and plugin work is fetched eagerly regardless of immediate user value.
findings.evidence: The initial load makes 108 requests; large Taboola, DoubleClick, AdSense, prebid, Facebook, Chart.js and mediaelement payloads contribute to 787KiB estimated unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional vendors on consent and visibility, load route-specific code only where used, and deprioritise background fetches until after primary content is interactive.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the page’s transfer budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 2,071,584 of 2,432,957 transferred bytes (85%) and 76 of 108 requests, led by ad and recommendation vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, self-host essential fonts/assets, and lazy-load remaining integrations behind explicit user value.

taskList.title: Fix article mobile reflow and reserve layout space
Gate and reduce the third-party advertising stack
Replace the blocking consent wall with a content-first compliant pattern
Deploy a complete security-header and cookie policy
Restore visible focus, accessible names and heading structure
Build dark and high-contrast preference themes
Optimise image sizing, formats and lazy loading
Use native top-layer and progressive transition primitives
Complete search and cinema indexing metadata
